headline: A short-term spending bill that keeps federal agencies funded through December 20, 2020, so the government does not shut down when the prior stopgap expires.
what_it_does: This joint resolution is a continuing resolution, a temporary funding measure. It provides money for federal agencies for fiscal year 2021 through December 20, 2020. Without it, the existing stopgap would expire on December 18, 2020, and the government would have a funding lapse. The bill keeps agencies open while Congress finishes the full fiscal year 2021 spending bills.

who_it_affects.how: They can keep operating at existing funding levels for a few more days instead of closing because their funding would have run out.
They avoid being furloughed or sent home without pay during a shutdown, since their agencies stay funded through the short extension.

who_it_affects.group: People who rely on federal services
who_it_affects.how: Programs and services run by federal agencies continue without interruption during the extension period.

when_it_takes_effect: Upon enactment on December 18, 2020, with funding available through December 20, 2020.
